Hello! During today's observation of the lesson on equivalent fractions, I noticed a major strength: the teacher effectively used multiple representations to help students connect concrete experiences to abstract concepts. For instance, the use of a cake analogy really helped students understand how fractions are parts of a whole. Students progressed to using key terms and explaining the concept of fractions by the end of the lesson.

One area for growth is differentiation. All students were given the same task, which means that some might have needed more support, while others could have been challenged further. A simple way to address this next time is to prepare two versions of the task: one with scaffolded support for those who need it, and an extension task for students who are ready for more challenge, such as comparing different fractions and explaining which is larger.

Keep up the great work! You're doing an amazing job facilitating learning, and with a few tweaks, your lessons can be even more effective for all students. Looking forward to seeing how you continue to grow and support your students!
